course.title: UAV Design: Foundations of Cyber-Physical Systems
course.subtitle: Master the foundations of UAV design, cyber-physical systems, and autonomous control
course.description:
Step into the world of intelligent aerial systems and discover how drones are transforming modern technology. This course takes you on a complete journey from the basic design and operation of UAVs to the advanced computing and networking methods that make them smart, connected, and autonomous. We begin with the foundations: frames, motors, sensors, flight controllers, and the logic of modular, open platforms that make upgrades and experimentation easy. From there, you'll learn how drones communicate over air-to-air and air-to-ground links, compare Wi-Fi and cellular (4G/5G) paths, and see when to use directional antennas, relays, or mesh networking for reliable coverage.

You'll then explore how drones collect, process, and share data using onboard computing, edge AI, and high-speed communication. Through clear explanations and real examples, you'll see how distributed computing, coordinated control, and 5G connectivity enable missions like search-and-rescue, inspection, mapping, and multi-UAV cooperation. We'll also connect communication and control through co-design principles: reinforcement-learning-based antenna alignment, swarm coordination, mobility models for safe airspace sharing, and practical strategies to reduce latency and energy use while maintaining link quality.

The final module focuses on airborne computing and AI: selecting Jetson/Intel boards, using containers and virtualization (Docker/KVM), and scaling intelligence across fleets with federated and coded computing. Each module builds on the last starting with drone architecture, moving through communication systems and control, and culminating in advanced edge computing and AI for resilient swarms. Whether you're an engineering student, researcher, or drone enthusiast, this course equips you with the knowledge to understand, evaluate, and build next-generation UAV technologies that compute, communicate, and collaborate in the real world.
course.welcomeMessage:
Hello and welcome to UAV Computing and Networking: From Basic to Advanced!

I'm excited to have you here. In this course, we'll explore how drones are evolving into intelligent systems that can compute, communicate, and collaborate. Take your time, follow each module in order, and make notes as you go — it will help connect all the concepts easily.

If you have any questions or feedback during the course, feel free to share them. Let's begin your journey into the world of next-generation UAVs!
course.congratulationsMessage:
Congratulations on completing UAV Computing and Networking: From Basic to Advanced!

You've gained a strong foundation in UAV hardware, communication, control, and airborne computing. I hope you're inspired to keep exploring advanced drone technologies and real-world applications.

Don't forget to leave a review and share your learning experience — your feedback helps improve the course for future learners.

Best wishes as you continue building and innovating in the world of UAVs!
learningOutcomes: Fundamentals of UAV systems: quadrotors vs. fixed-wing UAVs, flight controllers, sensors, and onboard computing
The concept of an Open Airborne Computing Platform modular design for research and prototyping
Basics of UAV communication: air-to-air and air-to-ground links, Wi-Fi vs. cellular networks, directional antennas
Networking opportunities and challenges: latency, bandwidth limits, energy constraints, safety, and regulations
Virtualization & Containers (Docker, KVM) for UAV computing flexibility and security
Control and Co-Design: how communication and control must work together, including reinforcement learning solutions
Distributed UAV computing: swarm intelligence, coded computing, and federated learning
Real-world applications: disaster recovery, emergency communications, agriculture, inspection, drone swarms, and smart cities
prerequisites: Basic understanding of computer networks and programming (Python/C++ helpful but not mandatory)
Familiarity with electronics or embedded systems is useful but not required
No prior experience with drones is needed — the course will guide you from fundamentals to advanced topics
targetAudience: Students in Electrical, Electronics, Computer, or Aerospace Engineering curious about UAVs
Researchers exploring drone technology and autonomous systems
Hobbyists and drone enthusiasts wanting to understand the technical side
Anyone excited about the future of drones, flying taxis, and smart city integration

instructor.name: Dr. Yan Wan, Dr. Junfei Xie, Dr. Kejie Lu, Dr. Shengli Fu
instructor.title: Professors of Cyber-Physical Systems
instructor.bio: With over 15 years of experience in UAV research and development, I've worked on cutting-edge projects in drone communication, swarm intelligence, and airborne computing. My passion is making complex UAV technology accessible to everyone.

modules.title: Module 1: Open Airborne Computing Platforms
modules.description: Learn how modern drones are designed as modular systems that combine control, communication, and onboard computing. This lecture covers UAV hardware basics — from frames and motors to controllers and sensors — and explains how open airborne platforms make it easier to test, upgrade, and integrate new technologies for real-world applications.

modules.title: Quiz 1: Open Airborne Computing Platforms
modules.description: Test your understanding of UAV hardware and modular platform design.

questions.question: What is the primary advantage of an Open Airborne Computing Platform?
options: It allows easy testing, upgrading, and integration of new technologies
It reduces the cost of drones to zero
It eliminates the need for sensors
questions.explanation: Open platforms provide modularity, making it easier to test new components, upgrade systems, and integrate emerging technologies without redesigning the entire UAV.

questions.question: Which component is responsible for stabilizing the drone during flight?
questions.explanation: The flight controller processes sensor data and adjusts motor speeds to maintain stable flight and execute commands.

questions.question: What type of UAV design is most common for hovering and vertical takeoff?
questions.explanation: Quadrotors use multiple rotors to achieve stable hovering and vertical takeoff/landing, making them ideal for many applications.

questions.question: Which sensor is essential for autonomous navigation and positioning?
questions.explanation: GPS/GNSS provides accurate positioning data that enables autonomous navigation and waypoint following.

questions.question: What does CPS stand for in UAV design?
questions.explanation: CPS stands for Cyber-Physical Systems, which integrates computation, networking, and physical processes in UAV design.

questions.question: What is the main purpose of redundancy in UAV systems?
options: To increase system reliability and safety
To make the system more complex
questions.explanation: Redundancy in critical systems (sensors, motors, controllers) ensures the UAV can continue operating safely even if one component fails.

questions.question: Which communication protocol is commonly used for UAV ground control?
questions.explanation: MAVLink (Micro Air Vehicle Link) is a lightweight messaging protocol designed specifically for communicating with drones and ground control stations.

modules.title: Module 2: UAV Communications and Networking
modules.description: Discover how UAVs communicate and form flying networks. You'll explore air-to-air and air-to-ground links, the use of Wi-Fi, cellular, and 5G/6G systems, and how drones can serve as relays, base stations, or connected nodes. This session also introduces networking challenges and modern solutions like SDN, NFV, and multi-access edge computing.

modules.title: Quiz 2: UAV Communications and Networking
modules.description: Assess your knowledge of UAV communication systems and networking protocols.

questions.question: What is the main difference between air-to-air and air-to-ground communication?
options: Air-to-air uses satellites, air-to-ground uses cables
Air-to-air is between drones, air-to-ground is between drone and ground station
questions.explanation: Air-to-air communication occurs between UAVs in a swarm, while air-to-ground links connect drones to ground control stations or base stations.

questions.question: Which technology offers the highest bandwidth for UAV communication?
questions.explanation: 5G/6G cellular networks provide high bandwidth, low latency, and wide coverage, making them ideal for data-intensive UAV applications.

questions.question: What role can a UAV play in extending network coverage?
options: None, UAVs cannot help with networks
questions.explanation: UAVs can act as aerial relays or temporary base stations to extend network coverage in remote or disaster-affected areas.

questions.question: What is a key challenge in UAV networking?
options: Limited battery life and energy constraints
questions.explanation: Energy constraints limit flight time and communication range, requiring efficient power management and protocol design.

questions.question: What is the purpose of MIMO technology in UAV communications?
options: To improve data rates and reliability using multiple antennas
questions.explanation: MIMO (Multiple-Input Multiple-Output) uses multiple antennas to increase data throughput and improve link reliability in challenging environments.

questions.question: Which layer of the OSI model is most critical for UAV real-time control?
questions.explanation: The Transport Layer is critical for ensuring reliable, low-latency delivery of control commands and telemetry data in real-time UAV operations.

questions.question: What is spectrum sharing in UAV communications?
options: Multiple UAVs using the same frequency bands efficiently
questions.explanation: Spectrum sharing allows multiple UAVs to efficiently use limited frequency resources through techniques like dynamic spectrum access and cognitive radio.

modules.title: Module 3: Networked Control and Co-Design
modules.description: This section brings communication and control together. You'll see how drones keep their antennas aligned using reinforcement learning, how they share information while moving, and how swarm coordination works when many UAVs fly together. We'll introduce models that explain how drones move randomly in real airspaces, and how safe integration is managed when multiple UAVs share the sky. You'll also learn about game theory and distributed control tools that help drones cooperate without collisions. By the end, you'll know how control and communication must be co-designed to make UAV systems safe, reliable, and scalable.

modules.title: Quiz 3: Networked Control and Co-Design
modules.description: Evaluate your understanding of control-communication co-design and swarm coordination.

questions.question: What is the purpose of co-designing communication and control systems?
options: To ensure both systems work together efficiently for safe and reliable operation
To reduce the number of sensors needed
To eliminate the need for pilots
questions.explanation: Co-design ensures that communication and control systems are optimized together, improving overall system performance, safety, and reliability.

questions.question: How can reinforcement learning help in UAV antenna alignment?
options: It learns optimal alignment strategies through trial and error
It only works on the ground
questions.explanation: Reinforcement learning algorithms can learn to dynamically adjust antenna orientation to maintain strong communication links as UAVs move.

questions.question: What is swarm coordination in UAV systems?
options: Multiple drones working together with distributed control
A single drone flying in circles
questions.explanation: Swarm coordination involves multiple UAVs working together, sharing information and making distributed decisions to accomplish complex tasks.

questions.question: Which technique helps prevent collisions in multi-UAV systems?
options: Flying only one drone at a time
Distributed control algorithms and collision avoidance protocols
questions.explanation: Distributed control algorithms enable UAVs to sense nearby drones and adjust their paths to avoid collisions while maintaining mission objectives.

questions.question: What is consensus in multi-agent UAV systems?
options: All drones must be the same color
Agreement on shared state information among UAVs
questions.explanation: Consensus algorithms enable multiple UAVs to agree on shared information (like formation shape or target location) through distributed communication.

questions.question: What is the role of a Kalman filter in UAV control?
options: To estimate system states from noisy sensor measurements
questions.explanation: Kalman filters combine multiple noisy sensor measurements to produce optimal estimates of UAV position, velocity, and orientation.

questions.question: What does MPC stand for in UAV control?
questions.explanation: Model Predictive Control (MPC) uses a model of the UAV to predict future behavior and optimize control actions over a time horizon.

modules.title: Module 4: UAV AI Applications
modules.description: Explore how drones act as flying computers. This lecture focuses on onboard AI processing, comparison of computing boards like Jetson and Intel, and virtualization tools such as Docker and KVM. You'll also learn how UAVs share workloads through distributed and federated computing, enabling smarter, faster, and more resilient swarm operations.

modules.title: Quiz 4: UAV AI Applications
modules.description: Test your knowledge of AI, edge computing, and distributed intelligence in UAV systems.

questions.question: What is the advantage of onboard AI processing on UAVs?
options: It enables real-time decision-making without relying on ground stations
questions.explanation: Onboard AI allows UAVs to process data and make decisions in real-time, reducing latency and dependence on communication links.

questions.question: Which computing platform is commonly used for AI processing on UAVs?
questions.explanation: NVIDIA Jetson boards provide powerful GPU acceleration for AI workloads while being compact and energy-efficient for UAV applications.

questions.question: What is the purpose of using Docker containers on UAVs?
options: To provide isolated, portable environments for running applications
questions.explanation: Docker containers enable flexible deployment of applications, easy updates, and isolation between different software components on UAVs.

questions.question: What is federated learning in the context of UAV swarms?
options: Each drone learns independently without sharing knowledge
Drones collaboratively train AI models while keeping data local
Learning is not possible on drones
questions.explanation: Federated learning allows UAVs to collaboratively improve AI models by sharing model updates rather than raw data, preserving privacy and reducing bandwidth.

questions.question: What is edge computing in UAV applications?
options: Computing only at the edges of the drone
Processing data close to the source (on the UAV) rather than in the cloud
Computing while flying at the edge of restricted airspace
questions.explanation: Edge computing processes data on or near the UAV, reducing latency, bandwidth usage, and dependence on cloud connectivity.

questions.question: Which deep learning framework is commonly used for UAV vision tasks?
questions.explanation: TensorFlow and PyTorch are popular deep learning frameworks that provide tools for training and deploying computer vision models on UAVs.

questions.question: What is SLAM in UAV navigation?
questions.explanation: SLAM (Simultaneous Localization and Mapping) enables UAVs to build maps of unknown environments while tracking their own location within those maps.
